about: Paztport version 4 over HTTP: conformance vectors. The keys, the `mesh` and `ops` policies and their proofs are the ones in v4.json, by name; only the `payment` key is new, derived by v4.json's rule (seed = SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-key:payment")), the same PKCS#8 and SPKI encodings, both base64url), and the boundary key below is SHA-256(utf8("paztport-http-v3-vector-boundary-key")), base64url. The v3 in these seed strings, and in those `rules.about` gives, is historical: version 3's vectors over HTTP used them, and keeping them keeps every key, root and nonce they derive unchanged. resultHash maps a status and body (hex) to the result hash. requestBinding maps a method, a target (the raw path plus `?` and the raw query when there is one) and a body (hex) to the request binding. headerNames maps a header name to whether it is Paztport's: it begins with `X-Path-`, compared case-insensitively over ASCII. A responses case is a request chain `sent` from gateway to orders to payment, with the blocks `sentBlocks` sent beside it, one per stamp, and the `responseHeader` payment returned; the caller `orders` checks it against `status` and `body` (hex) with the proof that the v4.json `policy` it names holds for `proofRoute`, as a verifier that acts on the extensions in `actsOn` and carries the names in `allowedExtensions` (null for unset, which carries any name), whose policy window ends at `policyNotAfter` and whose clock reads `now`, running the check `uses` times against one nonce cache of nonceTtlMs that already holds `spent` (none when absent), each nonce key the JCS text of its array of strings. It expects the last result, {reason, suspectSvc, suspectInst, handOver, resultHash}: handOver is null unless the reason is OK, and then has one member per name in actsOn ({} where actsOn is empty), each an array of {svc, items}, one per stamp of the sent chain and then the response stamp, items null where the stamp's block does not name the extension, as v4.json's verify cases record it. The responses cases on the `ops` policy run on a chain that names the operation each hop invokes (`orders#createOrder`, then `payment#charge`), with the proof for that route. The last three name `material` in place of `policy` and run on `rules.material.shop-keys`: each is a chain `sent` from gateway to orders naming `orders#reserve` and the `responseHeader` orders returned, which the caller `gateway` checks with `key`, the key value of the target sent. boundaryInfluence is the influence an egress sends to another organisation: under the boundary `key`, for `rid`, the partner entry `rcv` and the `egress`, the `input` entries reduce to `reduced`, with one salt (base64url) per (cls, owner) group in `salts`; each `openings` case is a `sent` entry and an `opening`, with its JCS bytes in `body` (hex), which the replay reads, and `opens` says whether it opens. `operations` holds `table`, an operation table as a `file` (its text) and `value`, with its `opsHash` and the `route` a root covers it as; `shared`, payment's table, an entrance with two operations told apart by a query condition, in the same form; `keyed`, a table whose operations declare keys, in the same form; `refused`, table files a reader refuses; `match`, a method, a raw path and a raw query (null for none) against a table `file` and the operation name it gives, null for none; `keys`, cases giving a call's operation in `keyed` and its key value, null for none; and `receive`, a request entered at `orders` through the HTTP receiver under enforce, on the v4.json `policy` or the `rules.material` it names, against a nonce cache that already holds `spent` (none when absent), whose chain's first stamp names `orders` or an operation of it, its `X-Path-Extensions` one empty block per stamp, with the `operation` the framework dispatches to (null for none), the receiver's `actsOn` and `allowedExtensions` as above, and the `refusal` it expects (null when the request is served). Every `receive` case on the `ops` policy carries the proof of `gateway/orders#createOrder`, whatever its chain names; those naming `material` carry its proof of `gateway/orders#reserve`, and the receiver holds `keyed` as its own table. `rules` holds the HTTP rules a receiver, a caller, a partner and an egress follow, and its `about` says how its cases read. boundaryInfluence, and every `rules` case whose `actsOn` (a partner's or an egress's own, for those kinds) names influence, need the influence extension's rules, since a service that acts on it reads each item it is handed under that name. responses names influence only as an opaque name and needs none, nor do the rest of the file and the `rules` cases whose `actsOn` is empty, but for the entry the egress that acts on nothing records for the partner's reply, in its `added`. Ed25519 is deterministic, so the file is reproduced byte for byte. Java writes and replays this file, and Go replays it; the TypeScript SDK has no HTTP binding, so it does not replay it.

rules.about: The HTTP rules the spec requires of a receiver, a caller, a partner and an egress, each case an input and the answer the spec gives. A key is looked up by name here, then in this file's top-level `keys`, then in v4.json; each new one is derived by v4.json's rule. A `material` is one organisation's policy key (by name), its signed root and signed keyring, each with its notAfter, the proofs of its routes and, for a partner, its entry service and reply certificate. Each root's tree has depth 1, its two routes filling both leaves with salts by v4.json's rule, so it has no padding; its rootId is "v" and the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256(utf8("paztport-http-v3-vector-root:" + tree)), for the vectors only. `handshakes` holds handshake requests on the shop's material, each nonce the first 16 bytes (15 for `short-nonce`) of SHA-256(utf8("paztport-http-v3-vector-nonce:" + name)), base64url, and `handshakeBodies` each request's JCS bytes; `peers` holds client certificates, each with the address it connects from. Bodies and certificates are hex, and headers are their values as sent. A receiver case enters `request` at `service` `uses` times against one nonce cache that already holds `spent`, each key the JCS text of its array of strings, the service's verifier, when it has one, pinned to `material`, and `expected` is the last entry's answer. The service acts on the extensions in `actsOn` and carries the names in `allowedExtensions` (null for unset, which carries any name), with a verifier or without one. Its `mode` is `enforce` or `audit`; `off`, a hop that verifies requests but whose deployment has switched it off; or null, a service that verifies no requests under a mode. Unless its name says otherwise, a case's chain is gateway's stamp to orders, then orders' to payment, and each hop's block names `influence`, with `[]` when the hop added nothing. The answer is the `refusal` (null when the request is served); `verified`, whether the request is served as having passed the live order at this service (false for every refusal); `handedOn`, what the service is handed, null for nothing, else one member per name in `actsOn` ({} where `actsOn` is empty), each an array of {svc, items}, one per stamp, items null where the stamp's block does not name the extension; and `attests`. Then the handler, having read the entries in `read`, asks two questions, at a service that acts on `influence`, as every receiver here does unless its `actsOn` says otherwise: `publicWrite`, the reason a guarded public write to a destination whose owner is `destinationOwner` gets; and `trustedRecord`, whether a trusted record may be written. A refused request runs no handler, and a service that does not act on `influence` asks neither question, so both are null then; work outside any request (a null `request`) asks only for the trusted record. A caller case is `caller` calling payment after `inbound`, the gateway's stamp, which came with the blocks `inboundBlocks`, its own block holding the entries in `added`, on `material`, holding the tables of the top-level `operations` that `caller.operations` names, as a caller that acts on `actsOn` and carries `allowedExtensions`, with a verifier exactly when `caller.verifier` is true; payment answers with `response`, and `expected` is the `rcv` of the stamp the caller signed, the check's `reason` (null where the caller has no verifier), whether the caller `refused` the response, and the `influence` entries the response adds. A partner case runs `steps` in order against one partner on `material`, which pins the policy keys `pinned`, takes the egress services `clientOrigins` as allowed origins, switches off `unsafeDisabled` for unsafe sessions, keeps at most `maxSessionsPerPeer` sessions per peer, each until no call has used it for `sessionIdleMs`, and acts on `actsOn` and carries `allowedExtensions` as a receiver does; its clock reads each step's `at`. A handshake step posts, from the client certificate `peer`, the `handshakeBodies` entry its `request` names, or `body` where `request` is null, and `as` names the session it opens, since the partner picks the id; it expects the HTTP `status`, the `error`, and for a session opened its `sessionStatus`, its `disabled` endpoints and the `extensions` the reply lists. A call step sends `method` `target` with `body` from the client certificate `peer`, naming its `session` by a handshake's `as` (`of`), as a literal (`id`), as an `X-Path-Session` value sent as written (`header`), or not at all (null), with `proofHeader` and `extensionsHeader` as given; its `stamp`, when there is one, is a boundary stamp with the fields given, signed as the step runs with the key `key`, in the session its `sess` names, over the binding of the call's method and target with the stamp's own `body`, and committing to `block`. A call may carry `read`, what the handler reads once it is accepted, and `destinationOwner`, which has the handler ask about a guarded public write as a receiver case's does. It expects the `refusal` (an unsafe session's switched-off endpoint, by `routePattern`, included), whether it is served `attested`, `handedOn` as a receiver case records it, `publicWrite` where the call carries `destinationOwner`, and `trustedRecord`, both null for a refusal. An egress case enters `inbound`, a receiver case's inputs (null for work outside any request), at the egress `egress`, which acts on `actsOn` and carries `allowedExtensions` as a receiver does, requires `requires` of the partner and goes on without them when `continueWithout` is true, and posts each of `posts` to `partnerScript`: a partner that answers each full handshake with the next of `handshakes` (`attested` or `unsafe`, a genuine reply on the `psp` material; `notFound`, a 404; `wrongKey`, a reply signed by and naming `stranger-policy`), the replacement as `replacement` says, every reply listing `extensions`, and each call with the next of `calls`. It expects each post's `outcome` (`answered`, with the `status` and whether the session was `attested`; `refused` by the egress's guard, nothing sent; `withheld`, no call made in a session that does not meet the requirement; `failed`, no session), all the partner `received` in order (a handshake, whether it had a client root; a call, its session and the session its stamp was made in, each the position of the handshake whose reply issued it, its stamps without `sess` and `sig`, its proof and its `blocks`), and the entries the request `added` at the egress. A boundary block's entries are blinded under the boundary key as `boundaryInfluence` pins it, for the partner `psp`, the egress `payment` and the rid of the stamp that commits to the block: in an egress case, and in `partnerTrustedRecord`'s stamps, which carry what a partner receives. The other partner kinds' stamps carry entries as a hop inside the mesh records them.
